usages.explain: Used by the speaker as a conjunction to negate speculation in the opposite direction or other related speculation by the listener after the speaker has presented something.

examples.content: A: 漢字は難しいねえ。B: うん、でもそうかと言って勉強しないわけにはいかないしねえ。
examples.transcription: A: かんじはむずかしいねえ。B: うん、でもそうかといってべんきょうしないわけにはいかないしねえ。
examples.mean: A: Kanji is difficult. B: Yes, but that doesn't mean I can't study.

usages.synopsis: .....そうかといって (そうかと言って), .....

usages.explain: Note: We use this sentence when assuming the preceding clause (the clause said before) is true. When using a sentence with this word, the following clause is often accompanied by "わけにもいかない".

title: そうかといって => but still
